# AudioBusVolume <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzBasic](BlitzBasic) · [Audio](BlitzBasic-Audio)

</div>


```blitzbasic
AudioBusVolume:Void bus:Int32, volume:Float32, fade_ms:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bus` | In | Int32 | required | A bus from [CreateAudioBus](CreateAudioBus), or `0` for the master bus. Anything else is a runtime error. |
| `volume` | In | Float32 | required | `1` is the full volume, `0` silence. Above 1 makes the bus louder. Below 0 is a runtime error. |
| `fade_ms` | In | Int32 | `0` | How many milliseconds it takes to get to the new volume. `0` (the default) changes it at once. Below 0 is a runtime error. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Sets the volume of a bus, at once or over a fade time. A channel is as loud as its own volume times the volume of its bus and of every bus that bus feeds, master included. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

## Differences

* The volume glides over every block of sound, so a fade has no steps, also when the program does not call Flip or Delay. [GetAudioBusVolume](GetAudioBusVolume) tells the volume.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
; Everything fades out over two seconds.
AudioBusVolume 0, 0, 2000
```
